properties.name: QuantLR
properties.short_summary: Developer of quantum-secure communication infrastructure, building quantum repeaters and entanglement-based networking technologies for long-distance quantum communication.

properties.name: Xanadu
properties.short_summary: Xanadu (founded 2016, Toronto) is the world's first publicly listed pure-play photonic quantum computing company (Nasdaq/TSX: XNDU, March 2026). It builds continuous-variable photonic quantum computers using GKP qubits in squeezed light: Borealis (2022) was the first cloud-accessible quantum advantage demonstration (Nature), and Aurora (2025, Nature) is the first modular networked photonic quantum computer with 12 logical qubits across four server racks. Xanadu also develops PennyLane (35,000+ active users), the most widely used open-source quantum ML framework. The company has raised $552M+, including a $302M SPAC listing, and is targeting a fault-tolerant photonic data centre by 2029.

properties.name: Pasqal
properties.short_summary: Pasqal (founded 2019, Massy, France) builds neutral-atom quantum computers using arrays of rubidium atoms held in optical tweezers and entangled through Rydberg interactions, supporting both analog quantum simulation and digital gate-based computing. An Institut d'Optique spin-out, its founders include Georges-Olivier Reymond, Christophe Jurczak, 2022 Nobel laureate Alain Aspect, Antoine Browaeys and Thierry Lahaye. Its €100M (~$108M) Series B, led by Temasek in January 2023, funds a path toward 1,000-qubit machines and fault-tolerant architectures.

properties.name: Q-CTRL
properties.short_summary: Q-CTRL (founded 2017, Sydney) makes quantum technology useful through quantum control. Founded by University of Sydney physicist Michael Biercuk, it builds infrastructure software — Fire Opal (automated error suppression for 100+ qubit algorithms), Boulder Opal (control engineering) and Black Opal (education) — that improves the performance of quantum computers across many hardware vendors, and is a leader in quantum sensing for GPS-denied navigation. In October 2024 it expanded its Series B to USD $113M, the largest aggregate Series B for a quantum software company.

properties.name: QuiX Quantum
properties.short_summary: QuiX Quantum (founded 2019, Enschede; University of Twente spin-out) is Europe's leading photonic quantum computing company, building universal quantum computers on ultra-low-loss silicon nitride (TriPleX) waveguide chips that operate at room temperature. It set a world record with its 20-mode photonic processor (validated in Quantum, 2023) and was the first company globally to sell a Universal Quantum Computer based on photonics — including a €14M contract with the German Aerospace Center (DLR, 2022). The company has raised €20.5M+ in VC funding (Seed €5.5M, Series A €15M) plus EIC Accelerator support. Founders include Dr. Jelmer Renema (Chief Scientist) and Dr. Hans van den Vlekkert; CEO is Dr. Stefan Hengesbach (former CEO of Q.ANT).

properties.name: Google Quantum AI
properties.short_summary: Google Quantum AI (founded 2012, Santa Barbara CA) is Alphabet's superconducting quantum computing division. It achieved quantum supremacy with the 53-qubit Sycamore processor in 2019, demonstrated below-threshold quantum error correction with the 105-qubit Willow chip in December 2024, and claimed verifiable quantum advantage with the Quantum Echoes algorithm in October 2025. The division operates its own qubit fabrication facility and publishes the open-source Cirq framework, pursuing a five-milestone roadmap toward commercially useful error-corrected quantum computation by 2029.

properties.name: QuamCore
properties.short_summary: Deep-tech quantum computing startup developing a superconducting processor architecture designed to scale into the million-qubit regime within a single cryostat.

properties.name: Quantum Source Labs
properties.short_summary: Developer of scalable photonic quantum computing hardware using a hybrid photon-atom architecture to enable fault-tolerant, large-scale quantum systems.

properties.name: Rigetti Computing
properties.short_summary: Rigetti Computing (founded 2013, Berkeley CA; NASDAQ: RGTI) is a publicly traded superconducting quantum computing company that designs and fabricates its own processors at its Fab-1 facility in Fremont and delivers them via Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) and cloud marketplaces. It pioneered the Quil quantum instruction language and the Forest open-source SDK, went public via SPAC in March 2022, and has advanced through Aspen and Ankaa processor generations to the 108-qubit Cepheus-1 system (April 2026, 99.1% two-qubit CZ fidelity). In May 2026, Rigetti signed a letter of intent for up to $100 million in CHIPS Act funding from the U.S. Department of Commerce.

properties.name: ORCA Computing
properties.short_summary: ORCA Computing (founded 2019, London; Oxford spin-out) builds room-temperature, rack-mounted photonic quantum computers based on time-bin multiplexed quantum memories. Its PT-1 was the first quantum computer sold to a national defence organisation (UK MoD, 2022), and its PT-2 (2024) delivers ~40 qumodes using deterministic single-photon sources with deep NVIDIA CUDA-Q integration. ORCA leads a £11.6M UK government quantum data centre consortium and has deployed systems at the UK NQCC, PCSS Poland, and Montana State University. Founders include Prof. Ian Walmsley (Oxford/Imperial), Dr. Richard Murray (CEO), and Dr. Josh Nunn (CSO, inventor of the ORCA memory).

properties.name: Quantinuum
properties.short_summary: Quantinuum (formed 2021, Broomfield CO and Cambridge UK) is the world's largest integrated quantum computing company, created by merging Honeywell Quantum Solutions with Cambridge Quantum. It builds the highest-performing trapped-ion quantum computers using a QCCD architecture with all-to-all connectivity — the H2 (56 qubits) and Helios (98 qubits, record Quantum Volume of 33.5 million) — alongside a full-stack software business (TKET, Quantum Origin, GenQAI). Backed by Honeywell, JPMorgan, NVIDIA's NVentures and others, it raised $600M at a $10B valuation in 2025 and filed for a landmark IPO in 2026.

properties.name: Quancilla
properties.short_summary: Early-stage quantum software startup focused on simplifying the development and deployment of quantum algorithms through higher-level programming abstractions.

properties.name: Quantum Machines
properties.short_summary: Developer of universal quantum control systems (hardware + software) enabling coherent and real-time orchestration of quantum processors across different technologies.

properties.name: enQuantum
properties.short_summary: Developer of quantum communication infrastructure focused on practical deployment of quantum key distribution (QKD) and quantum-secure networking solutions.

properties.name: QuEra Computing
properties.short_summary: QuEra Computing builds neutral-atom quantum computers from arrays of individually controlled rubidium atoms, pursuing both analog quantum simulation and large-scale, error-corrected digital computation.

properties.name: IBM Quantum
properties.short_summary: IBM Quantum (est. 2016, Yorktown Heights NY) is IBM's quantum computing division operating the world's first public cloud quantum service (IBM Quantum Experience, 2016) and the largest fleet of superconducting processors. Its hardware roadmap progressed from 127-qubit Eagle (2021) through 433-qubit Osprey (2022) to 1,121-qubit Condor and 133-qubit Heron (2023), with Heron powering the modular IBM Quantum System Two. The division also publishes Qiskit, the most widely used open-source quantum SDK. IBM targets 200-qubit / 100 M-gate Starling by 2029 and a 2,000-qubit / 1 B-gate Blue Jay system by 2033.

properties.name: IQM Quantum Computers
properties.short_summary: IQM Quantum Computers (founded 2018, Espoo, Finland) designs and manufactures full-stack superconducting quantum computers for on-premises deployment at research institutions and HPC centres. Its tunable-coupler transmon architecture delivers greater than 99.5% two-qubit gate fidelity across 20–150-qubit systems, with 30+ computers delivered worldwide. The company raised $600 M in total funding through a $320 M Series B in 2025 and is pursuing a US dual listing at a ~$1.8 B valuation in 2026.

properties.name: Alice & Bob
properties.short_summary: Alice & Bob (founded 2020, Paris) builds fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computers based on cat qubits — driven-dissipative superconducting cavities that suppress bit-flip errors in hardware, claimed to cut error-correction overhead by up to ~200x versus transmons. An ENS/Inria spinout founded by Théau Peronnin and Raphaël Lescanne, it raised a €100M Series B (later extended by NVIDIA's NVentures), was selected for France's €500M PROQCIMA programme, and opened a €50M quantum cleanroom in Paris, targeting an industrially useful fault-tolerant machine by 2030.

properties.name: Q-Factor
properties.short_summary: Q-Factor is a Tel Aviv-based quantum hardware startup building a scalable neutral-atom quantum computer aimed at the million-qubit regime. It was founded in 2026 to commercialize decades of atomic-physics research from the Weizmann Institute of Science and the Technion, both of which remain shareholders.

properties.name: Oxford Ionics
properties.short_summary: Oxford Ionics (founded 2019, Kidlington UK) is a University of Oxford spinout building trapped-ion quantum computers around "Electronic Qubit Control" — integrating qubit control onto foundry-fabricated semiconductor chips and using on-chip microwave fields instead of bulky laser optics. Co-founders Chris Ballance and Tom Harty hold multiple world records for trapped-ion gate fidelity. In September 2025 IonQ completed its acquisition of the company for ~$1.075 billion, making Oxford Ionics IonQ's UK quantum-computing hub.

properties.name: Quantum Brilliance
properties.short_summary: Quantum Brilliance (founded 2019, Canberra, Australia) is an Australian National University spin-out that develops room-temperature diamond quantum accelerators based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in synthetic diamond. Its compact, 19-inch rack-mountable QPUs — the QB-QDK series — eliminate cryogenic infrastructure, targeting HPC integration and edge quantum computing. Key milestones include the world's first on-premises room-temperature quantum computer at Pawsey Supercomputing Centre (June 2022), deployments at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (September 2025) and Fraunhofer IAF (May 2025), a Cyberagentur contract with ParityQC to build the world's first mobile quantum computer by 2027, and a Series A totalling over USD $46 million. Co-founder Marcus Doherty (119-marcus-w-doherty) is one of the world's leading NV-center theorists.

properties.name: PsiQuantum
properties.short_summary: PsiQuantum (founded 2016, Palo Alto CA) is building fault-tolerant, utility-scale photonic quantum computers using silicon photonics manufactured at GlobalFoundries' high-volume semiconductor fab. Its fusion-based quantum computing (FBQC) architecture targets million-qubit systems encoded in telecom-band single photons. The company has raised over $2.3B including a $1B Series E (Sep 2025, $7B valuation) and a A$940M Australian government investment (Apr 2024). Co-founders Jeremy O'Brien and Terry Rudolph are in the DB; interim CEO Victor Peng (former AMD President) was appointed Feb 2026. Quantum Compute Centers are under construction in Brisbane and Chicago.

properties.name: Classiq Technologies
properties.short_summary: Developer of an enterprise-grade quantum software platform that automatically synthesizes high-level functional logic into optimized quantum circuits for deployment across cloud and hardware backends.

properties.name: Quantum Transistors
properties.short_summary: Developer of semiconductor-based quantum processor technology focused on scalable spin-qubit architectures.

properties.name: Universal Quantum
properties.short_summary: Universal Quantum (founded 2018, Brighton UK) is a University of Sussex spinout building modular, scalable trapped-ion quantum computers. Co-founded by Sebastian Weidt and Winfried Hensinger, it connects many silicon ion-trap chip modules via "electric-field links" and drives gates with globally applied microwave fields rather than individually aligned lasers, targeting million-qubit error-corrected machines. In 2022 its German subsidiary won a €67M DLR contract to build fully scalable trapped-ion quantum computers in Hamburg.

properties.name: Element Six
properties.short_summary: Element Six (founded 1946, Didcot, UK) is a De Beers Group company and the world's leading manufacturer of synthetic diamond and superhard materials, with over 1,900 employees across the UK, Ireland, Germany, South Africa, and the US. It is the primary global supplier of quantum-grade CVD single-crystal diamond for NV-center qubit research, selling the DNV-B1 and DNV-B14 product lines that provide engineered NV-centre density for quantum sensing, quantum computing, quantum networking, and room-temperature masers. Key quantum partnerships include IonQ (foundry-compatible diamond films for quantum memories and photonic interconnects, announced September 2025), AWS (quantum networking research collaboration), the University of Maryland Quantum Technology Center / Walsworth Group (magnetometry characterisation), and Orbray (wafer-scale 50 mm diamond substrates). Element Six was selected for the DARPA LADDIS and UWBGS defence programs (2023-2024) and made a strategic investment in quantum interconnect startup Lightsynq (acquired by IonQ in June 2025). The company's Global Innovation Centre is located at Harwell, Didcot, Oxfordshire, and its advanced US manufacturing facility is in Gresham, Oregon.

properties.name: NVision Imaging Technologies
properties.short_summary: NVision Imaging Technologies (founded 2015, Ulm, Germany) is a University of Ulm spin-out co-founded by quantum physicists Fedor Jelezko (113-fedor-jelezko), Martin Plenio, Ilai Schwartz, and Alex Retzker. The company applies quantum spin-control technology — originating from NV-center research on diamond surfaces — to produce hyperpolarized carbon-13 metabolic contrast agents for MRI. Its POLARIS platform uses parahydrogen-induced polarization (PHIP) to boost MRI signals by over 10,000x in under three minutes, enabling real-time visualization of tumour metabolism on standard MRI systems. By end-2025, POLARIS Preclinical was deployed at approximately 20 centres including Memorial Sloan Kettering and Technical University of Munich. Having raised USD $120 million total (Series A led by Playground Global, Series B anchored by Abbott with EIB venture loan), NVision rebranded as NVision Quantum Technologies GmbH in May 2026 and announced expansion into photonic quantum computing (PIQC platform) for drug discovery.

properties.name: Alpine Quantum Technologies
properties.short_summary: Alpine Quantum Technologies (AQT, founded 2018, Innsbruck) is a University of Innsbruck spin-off founded by ion-trap pioneers Rainer Blatt, Thomas Monz and Peter Zoller. It builds the world's leading 19-inch rack-mounted trapped-ion quantum computers — full systems (PINE, LYNX, IBEX Q1) that fit in standard data-center racks, run at room temperature and draw under ~2 kW. Its LYNX series set a European-record Quantum Volume of 32,768, and IBEX Q1, operated in Innsbruck for European data sovereignty, is available on Amazon Braket.

properties.name: planqc
properties.short_summary: planqc (founded 2022, Garching, Germany) builds neutral-atom quantum computers using atoms trapped in optical lattices, the first spin-off of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics within the Munich Quantum Valley. Founded by Alexander Glätzle, Sebastian Blatt and Johannes Zeiher, it has won major German government contracts — a €29M DLR award for a 100-qubit machine and a €20M LRZ project (MAQCS) for a 1,000-qubit system — and raised a €50M Series A in 2024.

properties.name: IonQ
properties.short_summary: IonQ (founded 2015, College Park MD) is the first publicly traded pure-play quantum computing company (NYSE IONQ), building general-purpose gate-based trapped-ion quantum computers spun out of work by Christopher Monroe and Jungsang Kim at the University of Maryland and Duke. Its systems — Harmony, Aria, Forte and Tempo — report performance in Algorithmic Qubits (#AQ), feature all-to-all connectivity and near-room-temperature operation, and are available across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. In 2025 IonQ reported a world-record 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity and rapidly expanded through acquisitions including Oxford Ionics ($1.075B), ID Quantique, Qubitekk and Lightsynq, building an integrated quantum-computing and quantum-networking business.

properties.name: Quandela
properties.short_summary: Quandela (founded 2017, Massy; CNRS C2N spin-out) is a full-stack French photonic quantum computing company specialising in semiconductor quantum-dot single-photon sources and MosaiQ-series photonic quantum computers. Its Belenos QPU (12 qubits, 99.6%/99.0% gate fidelity, 576 QOPS) was delivered to CEA's TGCC for EuroHPC as Lucy in October 2025 — the world's most powerful photonic QPU in an HPC supercomputing environment. Quandela provides cloud access via OVHcloud and its own platform (2,400+ users) and the open-source Perceval SDK. Co-founded by Pascale Senellart (CNRS, also in our DB as 180-pascale-senellart), Valérian Giesz, and Niccolo Somaschi (CEO), the company has raised €68.5M+ (Seed €15M 2021; Series A €53.5M 2023) and employs 130+ FTE across two production plants.

properties.name: Quantum Art
properties.short_summary: Developer of scalable, multi-core quantum computers using trapped-ion qubits.

properties.name: Oxford Quantum Circuits
properties.short_summary: Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC; founded 2017, Reading, UK) is a University of Oxford spin-out that builds and operates superconducting quantum computers for cloud delivery under a Quantum-Compute-as-a-Service model. Its patented Coaxmon architecture places qubit control on the reverse face of a sapphire substrate, enabling compact, low-crosstalk scaling. OQC was the first European quantum processor on Amazon Braket (Lucy, 2022), launched the 32-qubit Toshiko enterprise platform in 2023 alongside a $100 M Series B led by SBI Investment, and deployed its GENESIS logical-era system in a New York City data centre with NVIDIA in September 2025.

properties.name: eleQtron
properties.short_summary: eleQtron (founded 2020, Siegen) is Germany's pioneering trapped-ion quantum computing company, a spin-off from the University of Siegen's experimental quantum optics group. Its proprietary MAGIC (Magnetic Gradient Induced Coupling) technology controls ion qubits with miniaturized microwave electronics instead of complex laser systems, aiming for robust, manufacturable machines. In May 2026 it raised a €57M (~$61.5M) Series A led by Schwarz Digits, backed by an order backlog exceeding €54M.

properties.name: Qedma
properties.short_summary: Developer of quantum error suppression, characterization, and mitigation software designed to enable reliable execution of quantum algorithms on today’s noisy quantum devices.

properties.name: Infleqtion
properties.short_summary: Infleqtion (founded as ColdQuanta ≈2007, rebranded 2022) is a Boulder CO cold-atom quantum technology company building the Hilbert gate-based quantum computer, the Oqtant quantum matter cloud platform, and commercial cold-atom hardware modules. Founded by Dana Z. Anderson (JILA/CU Boulder), the company raised a $110M Series B in 2021 led by Baidu and has significant DARPA/DoD sensing contracts. It operates offices in Boulder, Chicago, and Oxford UK.

properties.name: Atom Computing
properties.short_summary: Atom Computing (founded 2018, Berkeley CA) builds gate-based quantum computers using nuclear-spin qubits in optically trapped ytterbium-171 atoms. Its AC1000 system — the first to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based platform (1,180 qubits announced October 2023) — features 1,200+ fully-connected physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, single-qubit fidelity >99.9%, and on-premises or cloud (Azure Quantum) deployment. A Microsoft partnership (September 2024) demonstrated 24 entangled logical qubits on record; the companies are co-building the "Magne" system for Denmark. In May 2026, Atom signed a $100 million CHIPS Act Letter of Intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce.
